findings.title: Device-limit denial is cached as success
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device key into the 29-minute local cache before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. On ErrDeviceLimitReached the first call correctly fails, but the cache entry is left in place and the next TagDevice for that same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache and returns nil. Authenticate treats nil as success, so anonymous access is granted and the device is never recorded. A client that retries once (or any later request within the TTL) bypasses the limit entirely. The cache is also not cleared on transient DB errors, so a failed write is treated as tagged and is not retried for 29 minutes. Set the cache only after a successful write, and do not treat a limit failure as a cache hit.

findings.title: Device limit is enforced only if the client sends a device id
findings.body: The new auth denial depends on TagDevice, which returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is missing, and Authenticate then issues an anonymous identity. The header is optional and client-controlled, so omitting it never consumes a slot and never hits ErrDeviceLimitReached. A caller can also mint device_limit distinct ids to fill the quota (locking out honest frontends that do send the header) and then drop the header to keep its own anonymous access. As written, the limit cannot cap anonymous access. Enforcement needs a server-issued identifier, or requests without a tracked device must be denied once the cap is reached.

findings.title: Provider signature change will not compile with existing wire code
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts anonstore.AnonStore and now requires db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a deviceLimit parameter. This package is constructed by the committed Wire injector (pkg/server/wire_gen.go), which is not updated in this PR and still calls the old signatures. The server build fails until wire is regenerated. Any other in-repo or enterprise caller that passed an AnonStore is also broken, and tests can no longer inject a fake store.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with the insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts rows in one session, then inserts in another, with no transaction, row lock, or unique cap. Concurrent anonymous logins that all observe count < deviceLimit all take the INSERT path and the table (and thus anonymous access) exceeds the configured limit. This is the common case when many new devices arrive together at the cap. The count and the insert/update need to be serialized (single transaction with a lock, or an insert that rechecks the cap) so the limit cannot be overrun.

findings.title: Device-limit failure is returned as an unclassified error
findings.body: When the cap is hit, Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel (a plain fmt.Errorf). That is not an errutil or authn error, so the auth middleware treats it as an unexpected failure and typically responds with HTTP 500 rather than a controlled 401/403 and a user-facing device-limit message. It also shows up as a server error in logs. Return a typed unauthorized/forbidden auth error so the client chain and HTTP layer handle it as an access denial.

findings.title: Limit tests miss the allow-existing path and auth enforcement
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only inserts a second, unknown device id against the store and expects ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never checks that a device already inside the 30-day window can still be updated once the cap is reached, and nothing covers TagDevice, the local cache, or Anonymous.Authenticate. Those are the paths that actually grant or deny access, so the cache-as-success bypass and the missing-header bypass are untested and would ship green.

findings.title: device_limit is not added to default config
findings.body: auth.anonymous.device_limit is read with MustInt64(0), but conf/defaults.ini (and the docs generated from it) are not updated. Operators have no documented default, comment, or sample for the new cap, and 0-means-unlimited exists only in the store's if deviceLimit > 0 check. Add the key to the [auth.anonymous] section in defaults.ini with that meaning spelled out.
